title: South China Sea — vessel collision claims and primary-record hygiene
lede: Viral clips allege deliberate ramming between a coast-guard cutter and a resupply craft in contested South China Sea waters. Multi-language accounts disagree on who initiated contact, whether water cannon preceded impact, and whether anyone was injured. Train operators to separate AIS tracks, official statements, and geolocated stills from nationalist dubbing and recycled footage.
stakes: Mis-attributed collision narratives can escalate patrol postures, insurance premiums for commercial traffic, and domestic pressure for force-protection ROE changes.
known: Competing coast-guard and fishing-militia narratives appear within hours of hard contact in the Spratlys.
Open AIS can place hull classes near a scene even when flags are spoofed or AIS is dark.
Primary hierarchy: maritime authority releases, wire with named officers, geolocated original video, then commentary.
open: Exact lat/long of impact and AIS status of hulls?
Is circulating video continuous or cut from two incidents?

claims.plain: Hard-contact incidents between state-linked vessels and resupply craft have occurred repeatedly in SCS patrol zones in recent years.
claims.why: Multi-year open reporting pattern; specific new incident still needs primary lock.

claims.plain: A single social video alone proves intentional ramming and legal fault under UNCLOS.
claims.why: Intent and legal fault require investigation.

claims.plain: Water-cannon use immediately before contact is established for this specific event.
claims.why: Often alleged; needs continuous footage or official log.

claims.plain: Casualty counts on messenger apps should default to 0 until named medical or SAR sources appear.
Commercial shipping risk premia can move on credible corridor disruption claims before fault is settled.
claims.why: Insurance is forward-looking; not proof of fault.

title: Sahel security realignment — junta statements vs independent casualty claims
lede: After successive coups, Sahel juntas issue victory and partnership statements while NGOs and local reporters publish conflicting civilian-harm tallies. Separate decree text, AU/ECOWAS communiques, and named-field reporting from influencer war maps that invent unit designations.
stakes: False victory or atrocity claims can freeze humanitarian access negotiations and misdirect diaspora fundraising.
known: Junta media systems tightly control official combat narratives.
Independent tallies lag and use different civilian definitions.
Foreign partner presence claims need MoU or basing evidence.
open: Are place names consistent with road networks?

claims.plain: Multiple Sahel states experienced unconstitutional changes of government in the early-mid 2020s, altering security partnerships.
A single Telegram map proves control of a named district today.
claims.why: Maps without methodology are narrative products.

claims.plain: Civilian harm claims require named organization methodology and date range before +1.
Foreign trainer presence is confirmed for every junta statement naming a partner.

title: Red Sea corridor risk — attack claims, AIS dark, and insurer notices
lede: Ship attack and diversion claims move markets overnight. Force primary hierarchy: company and flag-state notices, navy incident releases, AIS gaps — not anonymous missile cams with wrong coastlines.
stakes: False attack reports divert fleets, spike freight rates, and pressure escort coalitions.
known: Commercial operators publish advisories when risk thresholds change.

claims.plain: Southern Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb has been a high-risk commercial corridor during regional conflict spikes.
Every viral explosion video over water is a confirmed anti-ship missile strike on a named tanker today.
Freight and war-risk premium moves evidence market perception, not legal attribution of a specific actor.
Coalition escort presence for a given week is established by official task-force releases only.

title: Taiwan Strait — drill notices, ADIZ tracks, and invasion-meme hygiene
lede: PLA drill announcements and Taiwan MoD track reports create screenshot fog. Separate NOTAMs, MoD daily updates, and reputable defense open-source from D-Day-tomorrow meme calendars.
stakes: False invasion clocks move markets, fuel hate targeting, and degrade civil-defense readiness messaging.
known: Taiwan MoD publishes activity summaries during tension spikes.
NOTAMs and maritime danger areas are primary for exercise boxes.
Amphibious invasion logistics claims need force-structure literacy.
open: Is the track screenshot from a different day?

claims.plain: Cross-strait military activity spikes are publicly reported by Taiwan authorities during major PLA exercises.
A viral countdown graphic is evidence of an imminent full-scale invasion date.
Exercise danger areas can be cross-checked via aviation/maritime notices when published.
Sortie counts on social cards match official tallies without citation.

title: Arctic sea lanes — dual-use basing claims and commercial ice data
lede: Arctic militarization posts mix commercial ice charts, dual-use port investments, and genuine military infrastructure. Bind basing claims to ministry primary or satellite-derived analysis with stated methods.
stakes: Overstated basing distorts alliance debates; understated basing misses dual-use logistics realities.
known: Sea-ice extent products are scientific primary for navigability seasons.
Port dual-use is a policy judgment needing facility-level evidence.
National Arctic strategies state intent, not completed basing.

claims.plain: Arctic navigability windows are constrained by seasonal ice; open products track multi-year change.
Every new Arctic port photo is a secret naval base.
Declared national Arctic strategies should be cited when claiming strategy shifts.
claims.why: Strategy documents are primary for intent.

claims.plain: Year-round container service on the NSR is routine for all vessel classes.

title: Western Balkans border flashpoint — municipal decrees vs clash videos
lede: Local decree fights, license-plate rules, and roadblock videos reheat faster than diplomatic statements. Lock municipal and KFOR/EULEX statements before scoring war-restart claims.
stakes: Inflated clash narratives trigger diaspora mobilization and mis-rank civilian risk.
known: License-plate and municipal disputes have multi-year history.
International mission statements are primary for force posture.
Roadblock videos need continuous capture and location locks.
open: Is the video from this week?

claims.plain: Northern border municipalities have seen recurring disputes over administrative control and symbols.
A single clash clip proves general war has restarted across the Balkans.
KFOR/EULEX posture changes should be taken from mission releases.
Casualty figures on partisan channels match hospital logs.

title: South Caucasus corridor deals — treaty text vs victory broadcasts
lede: Corridor access deals are announced with maximalist language. Enforce treaty/MOU text over parade rhetoric; check whether open corridor means customs regime, peacekeeping, or road repair.
stakes: Misread corridor status misprices logistics bets and inflames displacement fears.
known: Ceasefire and delimitation texts are primary for territorial claims.
Road opening can mean temporary humanitarian access only.
Third-party monitoring language matters for enforcement claims.

claims.plain: Corridor and transit arrangements are defined by specific instruments, not slogans.
A parade speech rewrites an international boundary.
Humanitarian access windows may be time-limited even when roads are physically open.
All displaced persons have returned under the latest announcement.

title: Korean peninsula — launch notices, debris claims, and early-warning hygiene
where: Sea of Japan / East Sea ranges
lede: Missile claims arrive as alerts, ministry posts, and crater photos of uncertain provenance. Prioritize Japanese, ROK, and US Indo-Pacific releases before scoring range, warhead, or failure narratives.
stakes: False warhead claims panic publics; missed real launches undermine warning literacy.
known: ROK JCS and Japan MoD often issue rapid launch notices.
Apogee/range numbers on social cards invent precision.
Debris photos need geolocation and time-of-day checks.

claims.plain: ROK and Japanese authorities publicly report many DPRK projectile launches in near-real time.
A social graphic with exact MIRV count is authoritative without ministry sourcing.
Civil alert systems firing is evidence of official risk communication, not of city impact.
Failure vs success is settled within minutes on messenger channels.

title: Great Lakes conflict minerals — supply-chain claims vs mine-site verification
lede: Armed-group tax and blood mineral claims move ESG and sanctions debates. Require mine-to-export chain evidence, OECD due-diligence language, and named smelter audits — not map aesthetics.
stakes: False linkage can destroy legitimate artisanal livelihoods; missed linkage can fund armed actors.
known: OECD due-diligence guidance is the method spine.
Tagging schemes are partial, not perfect.
Armed control of roads can matter as much as pit ownership.

claims.plain: Eastern DRC mineral supply chains have documented conflict-finance risks requiring enhanced due diligence.
claims.why: UN Group of Experts / OECD framing.

claims.plain: A single phone brand is uniquely guilty based on one undated pit photo.
Smelter audit status is a relevant control point for refiners.
All artisanal production is illegally taxed this month in every territory.

title: Caribbean maritime migration — intercept claims, capacity, and due-process flags
lede: Intercept videos and mass expulsion claims outrun official Coast Guard and migration-agency stats. Separate operational releases, asylum-process rules, and hospital reports from influencer boat counts.
stakes: Inflated numbers harden policy; suppressed numbers hide capacity crises and rights violations.
known: Coast guards publish interdiction statistics with definitions.
Individual boat videos do not equal monthly totals.
Due-process claims need legal instrument and case-level primary.

claims.plain: Caribbean maritime interdictions are regularly reported in official statistical releases.
One viral boat video proves a record-breaking monthly total.
Asylum and protection claims require legal-process primary, not comment-section consensus.
All intercepted persons were economic migrants with no protection needs.

title: Regional grid disturbance — operator reports vs blackout memes
lede: A multi-state voltage event sparks blackout maps and cyber-attack claims within minutes. Force utility and reliability-coordinator primaries before scoring cause.
stakes: False cyber attribution triggers overreaction; missed physical faults delay mutual aid.

claims.plain: Bulk-power disturbances are documented through reliability reporting when thresholds are met.
A dark city TikTok proves nation-state cyber sabotage.
Mutual-aid crew movements can fit weather-driven faults without proving root cause.

title: Major bridge emergency closure — inspection orders vs collapse rumors
lede: Emergency bridge closure after inspection races ahead of structural detail. Separate DOT orders from influencer collapse physics.
stakes: Panic diversions overload detours; delayed closures risk lives.

claims.plain: Emergency closure authority rests on the asset owner/DOT order text.
A photo of rust alone proves immediate collapse tonight.
Detour travel-time claims should cite DOT or probe data.

title: Container port congestion — AIS dwell vs supply-chain collapse rhetoric
lede: Anchorage counts and dwell charts are real metrics often misused as civilizational collapse proof.
stakes: Misread congestion distorts inventory policy and labor narratives.

claims.plain: Port authorities publish throughput and dwell statistics as operational evidence.
Anchorage photos prove permanent national supply-chain failure.
Chassis shortages can raise dwell without a single root cause.

title: Rail hazmat derailment — NTSB/PHMSA vs plume apps
lede: Derailment videos spawn chemical plume claims. Prioritize NTSB prelim, PHMSA commodity data, and local EMA orders.
stakes: Wrong chemical ID drives wrong shelter-in-place behavior.
known: Plume apps are models not measurements.

claims.plain: NTSB preliminary notices are primary for early accident framing.
A color-of-smoke guess identifies the exact chemical with certainty.
Shelter-in-place orders should be followed from EMA channels.

title: H5N1 in dairy cattle — USDA/CDC updates vs farm rumor mills
lede: Animal health detections and sporadic human cases generate pasteurization myths. Bind claims to USDA APHIS and CDC updates.
stakes: False food-safety panic vs under-prepared occupational risk.
known: Pasteurization science is settled for milk safety claims.
Farm worker PPE guidance is occupational primary.

claims.plain: USDA/CDC situation updates are primary for detection counts when specifically cited.
Grocery milk is unsafe nationwide because of a single herd detection.
Occupational exposure risk for dairy workers is distinct from retail food risk.

title: Hospital ransomware diversion — HHS notices vs ER chaos clips
lede: Diversion status and downtime procedures are operational facts often replaced by hallway panic videos of unknown hospitals.
stakes: Wrong diversion claims misroute ambulances; denialism delays mutual aid IT.
known: HHS HC3 tracks health-sector cyber threats.

claims.plain: Diversion status is an operational declaration by the facility/EMS system.
A hallway video from an unknown hospital proves national hospital cyber collapse.
Downtime paper procedures can maintain emergency care at reduced efficiency.

title: Critical drug shortage — FDA list vs compounding rumors
lede: Shortage lists are primary; forever-shortage memes and unsafe compounding advice are not.
stakes: Patients ration meds; unsafe workarounds harm.

claims.plain: FDA drug shortage listings are primary for US shortage status of listed products.
Social advice to import unlabeled product is medically and legally sound.
Manufacturer discontinuation notices explain some shortages.

title: Municipal ransomware — payment claims and public-record outages
lede: City services offline claims need CIO/incident notices; Bitcoin paid rumors need appropriation or disclosure primary.
stakes: Rumor can move bond chatter; silence can hide resident service gaps.

claims.plain: Municipal incident notices are primary for service outage scope.
Anonymous leak site PDF proves payment completed.
911 impacts require public-safety confirmation, not app downtime alone.

title: Nationwide telecom outage claims — FCC reporting vs map screenshots
lede: Carrier outage maps and complaint spikes are not interchangeable with FCC outage thresholds.
stakes: Emergency calling failures are high-stakes; exaggeration erodes warning trust.

claims.plain: Carrier status pages are primary for acknowledged incidents.
Complaint-volume charts equal network failure percentage.
911 special procedures may be invoked during major outages.

title: Synthetic official video — platform labels vs authentication
lede: A viral minister announces clip lacks chain-of-custody. Use reverse search, original channel, and forensic notes — not vibes.
stakes: Synthetic orders can move markets and crowds.
known: AV artifacts are hints not proof alone.

claims.plain: Authentication starts at the official channel and contemporaneous transcript.
Any facial artifact proves state-sponsored deepfake.
Platform labels are secondary risk signals, not forensic conclusions.

title: Extreme heat emergency — NWS products vs mortality guess posts
lede: Heat advisories are primary for risk communication; death tolls need vital-statistics methods.
stakes: Under-warning kills; fake tolls polarize aid.

claims.plain: NWS heat products are primary for meteorological risk messaging.
A social death count without vital records is authoritative.
Cooling centers listed by city/utility are mitigations to verify.

title: Flash flood emergency — USGS gauges vs basement videos
lede: Gauge height and flood stages are measurable; undated basement clips are not hydrographs.
stakes: Wrong flood stage confuses rescue priorities.
known: USGS gauges are primary for stage.
NWS flood warnings name river points.

claims.plain: USGS gauge height is primary for stage at a station.
Any wet street video proves a 500-year flood.
Road closure lists from DOT/EMA are primary for motorist action.

title: Wildfire smoke transport — AirNow vs toxic cloud memes
lede: AQI methods differ between regulatory monitors and low-cost sensors; both beat uncalibrated sunset photos.
stakes: Sensitive groups need accurate guidance; hype causes unnecessary flight.
known: School outdoor policies reference AQI bands.

claims.plain: AirNow AQI is the public-facing regulatory-oriented index for US messaging.
Orange sky photo equals hazardous AQI without a monitor.
Low-cost sensors can inform hyperlocal patterns when corrected and sited well.

title: Regional bank stress rumor — 8-K/FDIC vs screenshot ledgers
lede: Deposit-flight claims need call reports, 8-Ks, and FDIC notices — not cropped mobile-bank screenshots.
stakes: Rumor can create the run it claims to report.

claims.plain: SEC filings and FDIC notices are primary for material US bank events.
A cropped balance screenshot proves insolvency.
Social deposit-flight anecdotes can be early warning but remain 0 until filings.

title: Sanctions evasion shipping — OFAC lists vs AIS dark lore
lede: Dark fleet narratives mix real OFAC designations with undated AIS tracks. Bind vessel IDs to designation lists.
stakes: Wrong hull naming creates legal risk; missed evasion undermines policy.
known: OFAC SDN is primary for US designations.
AIS dark is not automatic violation.

claims.plain: OFAC designation lists are primary for US sanctions status of listed parties.
Any AIS gap proves sanctions evasion.
Ship-to-ship transfer patterns can be investigative leads requiring multi-source lock.

title: Commodity squeeze claims — exchange notices vs influencer price targets
lede: Margin changes and delivery notices are primary; to-the-moon threads are not inventory audits.
stakes: Retail FOMO vs commercial hedger risk.
known: Warehouse stock reports vary by commodity.

claims.plain: Exchange margin and delivery notices are primary market-structure facts.
An anonymous inventory photo proves global shortage.
COT positioning is public data useful for context, not price destiny.

title: Ballot cure process — state code vs viral rejection piles
lede: Cure windows and rejection codes are statutory. Viral trays of ballots without chain-of-custody are narrative fuel.
stakes: Undermining lawful cure or hiding real admin failures both harm trust.
known: County canvass is primary for counts.

claims.plain: Ballot cure procedures are defined in state election code and county instructions.
A photo of ballots in a mailroom proves systemic fraud.
Provisional ballot rates can be audited via canvass documents.

title: Electronic pollbook outage — contingency paper process
lede: EPB downtime triggers paper pollbook contingencies. Separate official incident tickets from stolen election livestreams.
stakes: Lines and provisional ballots rise; rumor weaponizes normal contingency.
known: Incident duration should come from election office.
Video of a line is not a turnout model.

claims.plain: Election offices can lawfully switch to paper pollbooks under contingency plans.
Any EPB glitch proves intentional disenfranchisement of a named group without evidence.
Wait-time estimates need systematic measurement, not one camera angle.

title: AI robocall suppression claims — FCC/state AG actions
lede: Synthetic voice robocalls targeting voters generate enforcement actions. Bind claims to FCC citations and state AG complaints.
stakes: Real suppression harms turnout; false alarms dull response.

claims.plain: FCC and state AG enforcement actions are primary for regulatory findings when issued.
Any odd-sounding call is proven AI without analysis.
Traceback notes can support attribution leads.

title: App store remedy orders — court docket vs founder threads
lede: Injunctive remedy language lives in orders, not podcasts. Score compliance claims from docket entries.
stakes: Developers misread duties; platforms overclaim compliance.

claims.plain: Operative injunctive language is in the court order text.
A CEO thread rewrites the injunction.
Appeals can stay remedies; check appellate docket.

title: Frontier model eval leak — lab cards vs screenshot science
lede: Purported eval tables circulate without methodology. Prefer lab system cards and replicable harness notes.
stakes: Fake evals move policy and investor narratives.
known: System cards are lab primary when published.

claims.plain: Published system cards are primary lab disclosures when authentic.
An anonymous leaderboard screenshot is definitive science.
NIST AI RMF is a voluntary risk framework often cited in policy, not a statute.

title: Municipal biometric ban — ordinance text vs vendor marketing
lede: Ban/moratorium claims live in ordinance numbers. Vendor compliant badges are marketing until mapped to text.
stakes: Agencies over-install; activists over-claim bans.
known: Ordinance number and effective date matter.

claims.plain: Municipal ordinance text is primary for local biometric restrictions.
A vendor slide deck proves legal compliance.
State preemption may limit local bans — check state code.

title: Open-weight model export controls — BIS rules vs Discord policy
lede: Export control claims need Federal Register / BIS rule text. Community myths invent license exceptions.
stakes: Developers risk violations; overclaim chills legitimate research.
known: Open release is not always uncontrolled.

claims.plain: BIS rule text and Federal Register notices are primary for US export controls.
A Discord pin is an authoritative license exception.
Model cards stating parameter counts help classification discussions but are not legal advice.
